clue.text: "Scrambled Eggs" Beatles Paul initially hit on over plateful … ?

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are beaten up, so the words that follow are beaten into a new order
initially means only the opening letter of the name Paul is used

parts.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A nod to Paul McCartney's working title for Yesterday, Scrambled Eggs, which came to him and turned into a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' shuffles EGGS, BEATLES, P (the opening letter of Paul), HIT, ON and O (over) into the eighteen letters. The trailing dots carry the Beatles story into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian pasta dish with meat sauce is served as a heaped plateful.

clue.text: One kicked off premises by Smollett's upwardly-mobile clog!

indicators.note: in a down clue moving upwards reads the letters from bottom to top
kicked off means thrown out, so the letter goes

parts.note: Tobias was the forename of the novelist Smollett, the name placed before his surname
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone is booted out of a property by a social-climbing Smollett character, with a clog as the weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicked off' drops I from TOBIAS to give TOBAS; 'upwardly-mobile' reverses it. Tobias Smollett was an 18th-century Scottish novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden shoe worn by French peasants is a type of clog.

clue.text: Fish Hollywood location up the garden path

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: an eel is a fish
Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone is led up the garden path by a Hollywood fish story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses EELLA. 'up the garden path' looks like the idiom for being misled, but 'up' is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal avenue or walk lined with trees or hedges, found in a landscaped garden.

clue.text: Misdirected ball in box rapidly put away

indicators.note: in means one set of letters sits inside the other

parts.note: to box is to hit with the fist
OG stands for own goal, a ball sent into the wrong net

explanation.surface: A wayward ball lands in a box and is quickly cleared away.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating greedily and fast is slang for gobbling food down.

clue.text: Distracted drumming? Cozy Powell's dancing partner's rubbish as well

parts.note: Cozy Powell's hit single was Dance with the Devil, so his dancing partner is the Devil
tat is cheap junk
too means as well

explanation.surface: Drummer Cozy Powell's dancing partner is dismissed as rubbish too.
explanation.walkthrough: Cozy Powell was a British rock drummer whose 1973 instrumental hit was Dance with the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the idle tapping of fingers or feet that a bored or absent-minded person does.

clue.text: I make an impression on title wrestling with enemy, but it won't change things

indicators.note: on means the first pieces sit ahead of what follows

parts.note: a dent is an impression made in a surface

indicators.note: wrestling means grappling and twisting, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A wrestler boasts of making a mark on the title while grappling a foe, yet nothing changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestling with' mixes TITLE and ENEMY into ITYELEMENT. The answer is a maths term: combining anything with it leaves that thing unchanged, like adding zero.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra this is the member of a set that leaves every other member unaltered when combined with it.

clue.text: … Yesterday's covers for Romans to impress?

definitions.note: garments worn in times gone by

parts.note: taken as written
in American slang, to gas someone is to thrill or impress them

explanation.surface: Following on from the Beatles clue, it pictures cover versions of Yesterday trying to impress a Roman audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yesterday' looks like the Beatles song again, but here it just means the past: the robes Romans wore long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome was their everyday outer garment, a covering of the past.

clue.text: Dick Fox with these timekeepers in nursery rhymes

definitions.text: Dick Fox with these timekeepers in nursery rhymes

parts.words: Dick Fox with these timekeepers in nursery rhymes
parts.note: the name Dick Fox rhymes with the answer, which is the nursery word for clocks

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings work together: the name Dick Fox rhymes with the answer, and children's word for clocks names timekeepers in the nursery. 'nursery rhymes' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children call clocks by the sound they make, so these are timekeepers in nursery talk.

clue.text: A foul-mouthed soldier's taking the biscuit

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the soldier's letters go around the rest

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald means coarse and vulgar in speech

explanation.surface: A soldier swearing a lot is said to take the biscuit, or be beyond the pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the biscuit' looks like the idiom for being outrageous. A Garibaldi is a British biscuit with a layer of currants.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Italian hero, it is a flat currant-filled biscuit.

clue.text: Earl visiting society do's on an unwanted roll

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a do is a party
re means on, in the sense of concerning

explanation.surface: An earl calls at a society party and is on a roll he would rather not have.
explanation.walkthrough: A roll here is fat around the waist, not a winning streak.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of fat round the middle is jokingly named after the extra wheel carried in a car.

clue.text: See 1
Top performers not providing us with a roundabout? So we hear

definitions.note: said aloud, roundabout is round about, meaning approximately

indicators.note: the word us is dropped and the letter a is supplied in its place

parts.note: performers under the big top make up a circus

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the best acts will not give them a roundabout ride, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works only by sound: 'roundabout' heard as 'round about', the Latin word for approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word placed before dates means approximately, that is round about.

clue.text: Crack A-Team carrying TNT pounded three times on walls for operational support

indicators.note: the walls of the first word sit around everything else, holding it in

parts.note: treble means three times over

indicators.note: carrying means one shuffled group holds the other in its middle
to crack something is to break it up, so these letters are rearranged
pounded means battered about, so those three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crack TV squad hauls explosives about, offering backup for a military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operational' points at the army, but the operation is surgical. 'Crack' and 'pounded' each shuffle their own word, 'carrying' nests the second inside the first, and 'on walls' wraps three times round the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons operate with the patient lying on this piece of furniture, so it supports an operation.

clue.text: See 11
Curious coastal lily is, I see, in a way to the left

definitions.text: in a way to the left

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: the letter C sounds like the word see

explanation.surface: A walker remarks on a strange flower growing by the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a manner of left-wing politics is behaving with leftist leanings.

clue.text: Rising American government's secret plant

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for government
arcane means secret or mysterious

explanation.surface: A rising American government's covert plant, a spy, is uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a planted agent, but it is the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall tropical grass grown for its sweet juice is a crop plant.

clue.text: A couple up on seventh heaven?

definitions.text: A couple up on seventh heaven?

parts.words: A couple up on seventh heaven?
parts.note: if paradise is the seventh cloud, two more steps up gives the ninth

explanation.walkthrough: Seventh heaven and the ninth cloud both mean bliss; the clue jokes that the second is two steps higher than the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on this is an idiom for feeling euphoric, just like being in seventh heaven.

clue.text: Line from Socrates (new translation)

indicators.note: a translation turns text into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A line from Socrates is given in a fresh translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like a quotation, but it means lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: A family line of descent is made up of forebears.

clue.text: Where girl may be involved with cheese tours?

definitions.text: Where girl may be involved with cheese tours?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so the letters of both words are mixed

explanation.surface: A girl going round cheese tours wonders which county she is in.
explanation.walkthrough: Mixing GIRL with CHEESE TOURS spells the county, and the whole clue describes it: this western English county is famous for its cheeses and its cheese-rolling race.
explanation.definitionFit: This English county is home to Double Gloucester cheese, so a cheese tour would take a girl there.

clue.text: "An England Captain in Defeat" interpreted on TMS as "Very Embarrassed"?

parts.note: to interpret is to read, and the past tense read is spoken exactly like the colour red

indicators.note: TMS is Test Match Special, the BBC radio cricket commentary, so the words are heard over the air

parts.note: Joe Root was England's Test cricket captain, so a beaten one is a beat Root, said as one phrase

explanation.surface: A headline about a losing England skipper is described by the radio commentators as deeply humiliating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read as a beat Root', heard on Test Match Special, the BBC radio cricket commentary, sounds like the phrase for blushing hard. Joe Root was England's cricket captain in 2017.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who blushes deep crimson with shame has a face the colour of the purple root vegetable.

clue.text: See 17
Divers he's taking to a lake resort

indicators.note: divers here is the old word for various or assorted, so the letters are sorted differently

explanation.surface: A man takes scuba divers to a resort by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like swimmers, but it is the old adjective meaning sundry. Lake Tahoe is on the California and Nevada border.
explanation.definitionFit: This Sierra Nevada lake is a well-known ski and holiday resort.

clue.text: Sheath that stops procreation

indicators.note: something that stops a hole sits inside it, so the letters sit within the next word

explanation.surface: A contraceptive sheath is something that prevents conception.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany this is a tubular sheath around a plant stem formed by fused leaf parts.

clue.text: Something fragrant from your local setter

parts.note: thy is the old or regional form of your
crossword setters refer to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A fragrant gift comes from the neighbourhood crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your local' suggests a pub, where the call is 'time', which the answer sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic herb is used in cooking for its scent.

clue.text: A bit of money I bet friend in Barcelona

indicators.note: only a bit, the opening letter, of the word money is taken

parts.note: a go is a try or a punt, as in have a go

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a little cash on a wager with a pal in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a pal, used by English speakers too, is what a friend is called in Barcelona.

clue.text: What about singer plugging remix of KeyNote chart topper?

indicators.note: plugging means filling a hole, so these letters go into the middle of the others
a remix rearranges a track, so these letters are reordered
about means turned round, so those two letters are read backwards

parts.note: eh is a request for repetition, meaning what?
Cher is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: A singer promotes a remixed track that tops the Keynote chart, and someone asks what about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chart topper' looks like one phrase, but 'chart' belongs to the shuffled letters and 'topper' alone is the definition. 'about' turns the interjection round before the singer joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: The final finishing touch that crowns everything sits on top, so a topper is an idiom for it.

clue.text: Square number (second last)

indicators.note: last means the letter is shifted to the very end of the word

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A puzzle note: square a number, with the second one coming last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like the maths instruction, but it means level, as in all square.
explanation.definitionFit: When the scores are all square they are level, with neither side ahead.
